title: “Google and Reddit do not own the Internet," web scraper says after court win
excerpt: Google's and Reddit's use of DMCA to fight web scraper is bizarre, expert says.
content_html:
Walling off the open web?

Google’s and Reddit’s use of DMCA to fight web scraper is bizarre, expert says.

After a big court loss last week, Google has confirmed that it won’t give up its fight to block AI bots from scraping its search results. And Reddit is weirdly along for the ride.

Curiously invoking the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), Google sued SerpApi last December. The search giant accused the web scraper of circumventing its anti-scraping technology and then selling content scraped from Google search results through an unauthorized “Google Search API” software service.

According to Google, the anti-scraping tech was in place to protect copyrighted content in search results. Allegedly, SerpApi’s circumvention threatened to disrupt Google’s relationships with rights holders, including some who license content to Google to appear in so-called “knowledge panels” that are displayed in some search results for well-known people or entities.

It was an odd use of the DMCA, since Google search results can’t be copyrighted. But Google was apparently emboldened to explore the legal theory after Reddit filed a very similar lawsuit in October, accusing SerpApi and Google-rival Perplexity of scraping Reddit content that appears in Google results.

In a blog, Google cited Reddit’s lawsuit when announcing its own challenge, which it said it filed as a “last resort” to block “malicious scraping” that violates rights holders’ choices over who can access their content.

Specifically, Google alleged that SerpApi’s circumvention violated its terms and made it impossible to profit from—or offset the cost of—“billions” of bot searches. And before it, Reddit claimed that SerpApi was evading two levels of security: Reddit’s own controls blocking scraping on its platform and Google controls blocking scraping of Reddit content in search results.

Meredith Rose, a senior policy counsel with expertise in the DMCA for a nonprofit public interest group called Public Knowledge, told Ars that Google and Reddit seem to be “sort of grasping at whatever tool is available” in the face of the sudden, continuous rise of AI scraping over the past three years. And while the way they’re using the DMCA is “bizarre”—and “not what the law had sort of contemplated as a use case”—she says it’s not “surprising.” Historically, the DMCA has been an effective tool to quickly stop disfavored content uses and force discussions around licensing, so turning to it may have been an obvious starting point, given Google’s goals.

But Google’s and Reddit’s unusual DMCA arguments don’t seem to be winning ones. Last week, a court took the somewhat rare step of granting SerpApi’s motion to dismiss very early on in Google’s lawsuit. In that case, the judge found that Google had no DMCA standing to sue SerpApi, since it didn’t own any of the content in the search results and has not shown that it’s acting on behalf of any rights holders.

“That does not happen terribly often,” Rose told Ars. “It really boiled down to Google didn’t allege enough about what it was protecting that was copyrighted.”

Likely the timing of that decision wasn’t great for Reddit, which faced a hearing on SerpApi’s motion to dismiss its lawsuit last Thursday. It’s unclear which way the court will rule in that case, but Rose told Ars that the Google ruling doesn’t bode well for Reddit since Reddit can’t claim that it is the content owner or exclusive licensee of content in search results.

“The judge in the Google case said, ‘Well, in order to have standing to bring a lawsuit under the DMCA, you can be the copyright owner or the exclusive licensee or the person who is deploying and manufacturing the technological protection measure at issue,’” Rose told Ars. “Reddit is none of those things.”

SerpApi is hoping that the fight will be over soon, telling Ars that the costly legal battle is worth sticking it out to defend the open web.

“The bottom line is that both Google and Reddit appear to be engaged in attempts to use the DMCA to wall off the open Internet by retroactively claiming control over content that they didn’t author and don’t own,” SerpApi told Ars.

Google’s last chance to keep fight alive

Although Rose agreed with SerpApi that, in granting the motion to dismiss, the court gave SerpApi a big win, the fight is not over yet, as Google has a narrow path forward to keep its war against web scraping alive.

Google acknowledged that search results can’t be copyrighted but argued that “knowledge panels” sometimes include copyrighted content that Google licenses from rights holders. If Google can amend its complaint to argue that rights holders directly authorized Google to use its anti-scraping technology to prevent unauthorized access to content, then Google may be able to block a very limited amount of SerpApi’s scraping.

Google’s spokesperson, José Castañeda, told Ars that Google plans to amend the complaint and is “pleased to see that the Court rejected nearly all of SerpApi’s legal arguments” otherwise attempting to dispute Google’s standing.

“We look forward to filing an amended complaint, as the Court invited us to do, and we remain committed to protecting our services and partners from unauthorized access,” Castañeda said.

However, Rose told Ars that Google has somewhat “talked themselves into a little bit of a corner here, both in this litigation and historically.”

For Google, it could be “very dangerous” to argue that the knowledge panel is “chock full of copyrighted material,” Rose suggested. Since the search giant doesn’t license all the content in the knowledge box, Google could risk future lawsuits if the act of algorithmically creating the knowledge box without licenses suddenly becomes viewed as infringement, Rose said.

“They have to make an argument somehow that there are parts of that that are reproductions of copyrighted material, but the only parts that are reproductions of copyrighted material are the ones they’ve explicitly licensed,” Rose suggested. “Otherwise, they’re admitting that they have been reproducing stuff without licensing it, and that gets them into another fair use fight that they probably don’t want to have.”

Google was given 21 days to amend its complaint, at which point it will become clearer how it plans to thread the needle to keep its DMCA fight going.

SerpApi calls fight “misguided”

Reddit did not respond to Ars’ requests to comment but claimed in a filing ahead of last week’s hearing that it was prepared to discuss how Google’s court loss impacted its case.

Perhaps notably, SerpApi said that Reddit was not among attendees in the courtroom. SerpApi did not comment much on Reddit’s arguments at the hearing but said that the judge appeared to be focused on the nuances of the legal questions. Most particularly, the judge seemed interested in whether Reddit’s agreement with Google actually authorized Google to protect its copyrighted content.

It would appear then that both courts have somewhat narrowed the fight to this key question, but SerpApi seems confident that neither Google nor Reddit can show evidence that scraping public search results harms rights holders.

Asked for comment on Google’s plan to amend its complaint, SerpApi told Ars that there may be little point in continuing to argue over “snippets of text that appear in Google’s Knowledge Panels” after Google launched its attack to supposedly defend “hundreds of thousands of publishers” that appear in search results.

“We hope Google drops this misguided attack on the open Internet, but if necessary, we are prepared to defend SerpApi, our customers, and our principles,” SerpApi said.

SerpApi told Ars that its business has continued to grow while it has fought the DMCA lawsuits but that its customers, including tech giants like Nvidia, Uber, and Adobe, have faced uncertainty as both cases have dragged on.

They “rely on SerpApi every day to provide structured access to search data, which is and has always been a lawful and legitimate business,” SerpApi said.

SerpApi’s right to defend open web, expert says

Beyond its own customers, people invested in the open web have also pondered what the impact of a Google win could be, SerpApi suggested.

“Of course, litigation is incredibly expensive and disruptive,” SerpApi said. “However, we feel strongly that platforms such as Google and Reddit do not own the Internet and that their attempts to weaponize the DMCA threaten all users of the open web.”

Rose told Ars that while SerpApi hasn’t necessarily “endeared itself to a lot of people,” she thinks that “they’re in the right from a policy perspective here.”

Ever since the summer of 2023—when a sort of “API apocalypse” began—publishers have been cutting off access to the open web, Rose said, by attempting to find ways to quickly stop high volumes of AI scraping like SerpApi does.

“This mass reaction to scraping” has caused a “re-enclosure of a lot of the web,” Rose said. And concerningly, that doesn’t just gum up AI training efforts, it also harms research, archiving, journalism, public health reporting, and other important work that depends on anonymous crawling and automated scraping at scale, Rose said.

SerpApi told Ars that it has gotten “overwhelming” feedback from its customers, researchers, and SEO providers in support of its efforts to defend against the Google and Reddit lawsuits. The web scraper is optimistic that the court will grant its motion to dismiss against Reddit and last week celebrated that Google’s lawsuit may only proceed on very limited claims.

In a win, SerpApi warned that Reddit planned to act as a “toll collector,” requiring payments for scraping when it doesn’t even own the content.

“Reddit seeks to consolidate its control over its users’ content so that it will be in a better position to tax that content. Reddit is not acting to protect its users; Reddit is clearing a path to exploit them,” SerpApi warned.

Similarly, SerpApi accused Google of asking the court to ignore that it’s the “largest scraper on the planet,” while agreeing to cut off other web scrapers from information that is “100 percent public.”

For Rose, there’s no winning for online users if, at the end of the fight, public access to data is cut off.

“It’s a very fraught time,” Rose said, acknowledging that it’s not just Reddit and Google but many publishers across the web that are currently tempted to use “whatever tool is available in the toolbox to tamper down” AI scraping.

Some publishers may be financially motivated, like Google and Reddit, while others may be protecting their infrastructure or taking a moral stance, Rose said. Whatever the motivation is, “it’s leading to this kind of broader ecosystem-wide consequence of re-enclosure,” she warned.

And although SerpApi expects to win, the problem with DMCA cases, she suggested, is that it can be difficult to predict the outcome.

“I’m very curious how this is going to play out with Reddit,” Rose said. “I’m always a little bit cynical because to some extent, whenever you get into the copyright realm, a lot of judges just decide it’s all vibes.”

Advance Publications, which owns Ars Technica parent Condé Nast, is the largest shareholder in Reddit.

Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

blocks.html_en: Likely the timing of that decision wasn’t great for Reddit, which faced a hearing on SerpApi’s motion to dismiss its lawsuit last Thursday. It’s unclear which way the court will rule in that case, but Rose told Ars that the Google ruling doesn’t bode well for Reddit since Reddit can’t claim that it is the content owner or exclusive licensee of content in search results.

sentences.en: Likely the timing of that decision wasn’t great for Reddit, which faced a hearing on SerpApi’s motion to dismiss its lawsuit last Thursday.
sentences.zh: 对于 Reddit 来说，这一决定的时机可能不太好，上周四 Reddit 就 SerpApi 驳回诉讼的动议举行了听证会。

sentences.en: It’s unclear which way the court will rule in that case, but Rose told Ars that the Google ruling doesn’t bode well for Reddit since Reddit can’t claim that it is the content owner or exclusive licensee of content in search results.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚法院将如何裁决该案，但罗斯告诉 Ars，谷歌的裁决对 Reddit 来说不是好兆头，因为 Reddit 不能声称自己是搜索结果中内容的内容所有者或独家被许可人。

blocks.html_en: “The judge in the Google case said, ‘Well, in order to have standing to bring a lawsuit under the DMCA, you can be the copyright owner or the exclusive licensee or the person who is deploying and manufacturing the technological protection measure at issue,’” Rose told Ars. “Reddit is none of those things.”

sentences.en: “The judge in the Google case said, ‘Well, in order to have standing to bring a lawsuit under the DMCA, you can be the copyright owner or the exclusive licensee or the person who is deploying and manufacturing the technological protection measure at issue,’” Rose told Ars.
sentences.zh: “谷歌案件的法官说，‘好吧，为了有资格根据 DMCA 提起诉讼，你可以是版权所有者或独家被许可人或正在部署和制造相关技术保护措施的人，’”Rose 告诉 Ars。

sentences.en: “Reddit is none of those things.”
sentences.zh: “Reddit 不是这些东西。”

blocks.html_en: SerpApi is hoping that the fight will be over soon, telling Ars that the costly legal battle is worth sticking it out to defend the open web.

sentences.en: SerpApi is hoping that the fight will be over soon, telling Ars that the costly legal battle is worth sticking it out to defend the open web.
sentences.zh: SerpApi 希望这场斗争能够尽快结束，并告诉 Ars，为了捍卫开放网络，这场代价高昂的法律斗争值得坚持下去。

blocks.html_en: “The bottom line is that both Google and Reddit appear to be engaged in attempts to use the DMCA to wall off the open Internet by retroactively claiming control over content that they didn’t author and don’t own,” SerpApi told Ars.

sentences.en: “The bottom line is that both Google and Reddit appear to be engaged in attempts to use the DMCA to wall off the open Internet by retroactively claiming control over content that they didn’t author and don’t own,” SerpApi told Ars.
sentences.zh: SerpApi 告诉 Ars：“最重要的是，谷歌和 Reddit 似乎都试图利用 DMCA 来隔离开放的互联网，追溯性地声称控制非他们创作且不拥有的内容。”

blocks.html_en: Google’s last chance to keep fight alive

sentences.en: Google’s last chance to keep fight alive
sentences.zh: 谷歌继续战斗的最后机会

blocks.html_en: Although Rose agreed with SerpApi that, in granting the motion to dismiss, the court gave SerpApi a big win, the fight is not over yet, as Google has a narrow path forward to keep its war against web scraping alive.

sentences.en: Although Rose agreed with SerpApi that, in granting the motion to dismiss, the court gave SerpApi a big win, the fight is not over yet, as Google has a narrow path forward to keep its war against web scraping alive.
sentences.zh: 尽管 Rose 同意 SerpApi 的观点，即在批准驳回动议时，法院给 SerpApi 带来了一场巨大的胜利，但斗争尚未结束，因为谷歌在继续打击网络抓取方面的道路很狭窄。

blocks.html_en: Google acknowledged that search results can’t be copyrighted but argued that “knowledge panels” sometimes include copyrighted content that Google licenses from rights holders. If Google can amend its complaint to argue that rights holders directly authorized Google to use its anti-scraping technology to prevent unauthorized access to content, then Google may be able to block a very limited amount of SerpApi’s scraping.

sentences.en: Google acknowledged that search results can’t be copyrighted but argued that “knowledge panels” sometimes include copyrighted content that Google licenses from rights holders.
sentences.zh: 谷歌承认搜索结果不受版权保护，但辩称“知识面板”有时包括谷歌从权利持有者处许可的受版权保护的内容。

sentences.en: If Google can amend its complaint to argue that rights holders directly authorized Google to use its anti-scraping technology to prevent unauthorized access to content, then Google may be able to block a very limited amount of SerpApi’s scraping.
sentences.zh: 如果谷歌可以修改其投诉，声称权利持有者直接授权谷歌使用其反抓取技术来防止未经授权的内容访问，那么谷歌也许能够阻止非常有限的 SerpApi 抓取量。

blocks.html_en: Google’s spokesperson, José Castañeda, told Ars that Google plans to amend the complaint and is “pleased to see that the Court rejected nearly all of SerpApi’s legal arguments” otherwise attempting to dispute Google’s standing.

sentences.en: Google’s spokesperson, José Castañeda, told Ars that Google plans to amend the complaint and is “pleased to see that the Court rejected nearly all of SerpApi’s legal arguments” otherwise attempting to dispute Google’s standing.
sentences.zh: 谷歌发言人何塞·卡斯塔涅达 (José Castañeda) 告诉 Ars，谷歌计划修改起诉书，并“很高兴看到法院驳回了 SerpApi 几乎所有的法律论据”，否则试图对谷歌的地位提出质疑。

blocks.html_en: “We look forward to filing an amended complaint, as the Court invited us to do, and we remain committed to protecting our services and partners from unauthorized access,” Castañeda said.

sentences.en: “We look forward to filing an amended complaint, as the Court invited us to do, and we remain committed to protecting our services and partners from unauthorized access,” Castañeda said.
sentences.zh: 卡斯塔涅达表示：“我们期待按照法院的邀请提交修改后的申诉，并且我们仍然致力于保护我们的服务和合作伙伴免受未经授权的访问。”

blocks.html_en: However, Rose told Ars that Google has somewhat “talked themselves into a little bit of a corner here, both in this litigation and historically.”

sentences.en: However, Rose told Ars that Google has somewhat “talked themselves into a little bit of a corner here, both in this litigation and historically.”
sentences.zh: 然而，罗斯告诉 Ars，谷歌在某种程度上“无论是在这次诉讼中还是在历史上，都让自己陷入了困境”。

blocks.html_en: For Google, it could be “very dangerous” to argue that the knowledge panel is “chock full of copyrighted material,” Rose suggested. Since the search giant doesn’t license all the content in the knowledge box, Google could risk future lawsuits if the act of algorithmically creating the knowledge box without licenses suddenly becomes viewed as infringement, Rose said.

sentences.en: For Google, it could be “very dangerous” to argue that the knowledge panel is “chock full of copyrighted material,” Rose suggested.
sentences.zh: 罗斯表示，对于谷歌来说，认为知识面板“充满了受版权保护的材料”可能是“非常危险的”。

sentences.en: Since the search giant doesn’t license all the content in the knowledge box, Google could risk future lawsuits if the act of algorithmically creating the knowledge box without licenses suddenly becomes viewed as infringement, Rose said.
sentences.zh: 罗斯表示，由于这家搜索巨头并未对知识盒中的所有内容进行许可，因此如果未经许可通过算法创建知识盒的行为突然被视为侵权，谷歌可能会面临未来诉讼的风险。

blocks.html_en: “They have to make an argument somehow that there are parts of that that are reproductions of copyrighted material, but the only parts that are reproductions of copyrighted material are the ones they’ve explicitly licensed,” Rose suggested. “Otherwise, they’re admitting that they have been reproducing stuff without licensing it, and that gets them into another fair use fight that they probably don’t want to have.”

sentences.en: “They have to make an argument somehow that there are parts of that that are reproductions of copyrighted material, but the only parts that are reproductions of copyrighted material are the ones they’ve explicitly licensed,” Rose suggested.
sentences.zh: “他们必须以某种方式提出论点，其中的某些部分是受版权保护材料的复制品，但唯一属于受版权保护材料复制品的部分是他们明确许可的内容，”罗斯建议道。

sentences.en: “Otherwise, they’re admitting that they have been reproducing stuff without licensing it, and that gets them into another fair use fight that they probably don’t want to have.”
sentences.zh: “否则，他们就承认自己在未经许可的情况下复制了一些东西，这会让他们陷入另一场他们可能不希望发生的合理使用之争。”

blocks.html_en: Google was given 21 days to amend its complaint, at which point it will become clearer how it plans to thread the needle to keep its DMCA fight going.

sentences.en: Google was given 21 days to amend its complaint, at which point it will become clearer how it plans to thread the needle to keep its DMCA fight going.
sentences.zh: 谷歌有 21 天的时间来修改其投诉，届时它计划如何继续其 DMCA 斗争将变得更加清晰。

blocks.html_en: SerpApi calls fight “misguided”

sentences.en: SerpApi calls fight “misguided”
sentences.zh: SerpApi 称战斗是“误导的”

blocks.html_en: Reddit did not respond to Ars’ requests to comment but claimed in a filing ahead of last week’s hearing that it was prepared to discuss how Google’s court loss impacted its case.

sentences.en: Reddit did not respond to Ars’ requests to comment but claimed in a filing ahead of last week’s hearing that it was prepared to discuss how Google’s court loss impacted its case.
sentences.zh: Reddit 没有回应 Ars 的置评请求，但在上周听证会之前的一份文件中声称，它准备讨论谷歌的法庭败诉对其案件有何影响。

blocks.html_en: Perhaps notably, SerpApi said that Reddit was not among attendees in the courtroom. SerpApi did not comment much on Reddit’s arguments at the hearing but said that the judge appeared to be focused on the nuances of the legal questions. Most particularly, the judge seemed interested in whether Reddit’s agreement with Google actually authorized Google to protect its copyrighted content.

sentences.en: Perhaps notably, SerpApi said that Reddit was not among attendees in the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 也许值得注意的是，SerpApi 表示 Reddit 并未出现在法庭的出席者之中。

sentences.en: SerpApi did not comment much on Reddit’s arguments at the hearing but said that the judge appeared to be focused on the nuances of the legal questions.
sentences.zh: SerpApi 没有对 Reddit 在听证会上的论点发表太多评论，但表示法官似乎专注于法律问题的细微差别。

sentences.en: Most particularly, the judge seemed interested in whether Reddit’s agreement with Google actually authorized Google to protect its copyrighted content.
sentences.zh: 最特别的是，法官似乎对 Reddit 与谷歌的协议是否实际上授权谷歌保护其受版权保护的内容感兴趣。

blocks.html_en: It would appear then that both courts have somewhat narrowed the fight to this key question, but SerpApi seems confident that neither Google nor Reddit can show evidence that scraping public search results harms rights holders.

sentences.en: It would appear then that both courts have somewhat narrowed the fight to this key question, but SerpApi seems confident that neither Google nor Reddit can show evidence that scraping public search results harms rights holders.
sentences.zh: 这样看来，两个法院都在一定程度上缩小了对这个关键问题的争论范围，但 SerpApi 似乎相信谷歌和 Reddit 都无法提供证据证明抓取公共搜索结果会损害权利人的利益。

blocks.html_en: Asked for comment on Google’s plan to amend its complaint, SerpApi told Ars that there may be little point in continuing to argue over “snippets of text that appear in Google’s Knowledge Panels” after Google launched its attack to supposedly defend “hundreds of thousands of publishers” that appear in search results.

sentences.en: Asked for comment on Google’s plan to amend its complaint, SerpApi told Ars that there may be little point in continuing to argue over “snippets of text that appear in Google’s Knowledge Panels” after Google launched its attack to supposedly defend “hundreds of thousands of publishers” that appear in search results.
sentences.zh: 当被问及对谷歌修改投诉的计划发表评论时，SerpApi 告诉 Ars，在谷歌发起攻击以保护搜索结果中出现的“数十万出版商”之后，继续争论“谷歌知识面板中出现的文本片段”可能没有什么意义。

blocks.html_en: “We hope Google drops this misguided attack on the open Internet, but if necessary, we are prepared to defend SerpApi, our customers, and our principles,” SerpApi said.

sentences.en: “We hope Google drops this misguided attack on the open Internet, but if necessary, we are prepared to defend SerpApi, our customers, and our principles,” SerpApi said.
sentences.zh: SerpApi 表示：“我们希望谷歌放弃对开放互联网的这种误导性攻击，但如有必要，我们准备捍卫 SerpApi、我们的客户和我们的原则。”

blocks.html_en: SerpApi told Ars that its business has continued to grow while it has fought the DMCA lawsuits but that its customers, including tech giants like Nvidia, Uber, and Adobe, have faced uncertainty as both cases have dragged on.

sentences.en: SerpApi told Ars that its business has continued to grow while it has fought the DMCA lawsuits but that its customers, including tech giants like Nvidia, Uber, and Adobe, have faced uncertainty as both cases have dragged on.
sentences.zh: SerpApi 告诉 Ars，在应对 DMCA 诉讼的同时，其业务仍在持续增长，但由于两起案件都拖延，其客户，包括 Nvidia、Uber 和 Adob​​e 等科技巨头，都面临着不确定性。

blocks.html_en: They “rely on SerpApi every day to provide structured access to search data, which is and has always been a lawful and legitimate business,” SerpApi said.

sentences.en: They “rely on SerpApi every day to provide structured access to search data, which is and has always been a lawful and legitimate business,” SerpApi said.
sentences.zh: SerpApi 表示，他们“每天都依靠 SerpApi 提供对搜索数据的结构化访问，这一直是合法且合法的业务”。

blocks.html_en: SerpApi’s right to defend open web, expert says

sentences.en: SerpApi’s right to defend open web, expert says
sentences.zh: 专家称 SerpApi 有权捍卫开放网络

blocks.html_en: Beyond its own customers, people invested in the open web have also pondered what the impact of a Google win could be, SerpApi suggested.

sentences.en: Beyond its own customers, people invested in the open web have also pondered what the impact of a Google win could be, SerpApi suggested.
sentences.zh: SerpApi 表示，除了自己的客户之外，投资开放网络的人们也在思考谷歌获胜可能带来的影响。

blocks.html_en: “Of course, litigation is incredibly expensive and disruptive,” SerpApi said. “However, we feel strongly that platforms such as Google and Reddit do not own the Internet and that their attempts to weaponize the DMCA threaten all users of the open web.”

sentences.en: “Of course, litigation is incredibly expensive and disruptive,” SerpApi said.
sentences.zh: SerpApi 表示：“当然，诉讼成本高昂且具有破坏性。”

sentences.en: “However, we feel strongly that platforms such as Google and Reddit do not own the Internet and that their attempts to weaponize the DMCA threaten all users of the open web.”
sentences.zh: “然而，我们强烈认为，谷歌和 Reddit 等平台并不拥有互联网，他们试图将 DMCA 武器化，威胁到开放网络的所有用户。”

blocks.html_en: Rose told Ars that while SerpApi hasn’t necessarily “endeared itself to a lot of people,” she thinks that “they’re in the right from a policy perspective here.”

sentences.en: Rose told Ars that while SerpApi hasn’t necessarily “endeared itself to a lot of people,” she thinks that “they’re in the right from a policy perspective here.”
sentences.zh: Rose 告诉 Ars，虽然 SerpApi 不一定“受到很多人的喜爱”，但她认为“从政策角度来看，他们是正确的。”

blocks.html_en: Ever since the summer of 2023—when a sort of “API apocalypse” began—publishers have been cutting off access to the open web, Rose said, by attempting to find ways to quickly stop high volumes of AI scraping like SerpApi does.

sentences.en: Ever since the summer of 2023—when a sort of “API apocalypse” began—publishers have been cutting off access to the open web, Rose said, by attempting to find ways to quickly stop high volumes of AI scraping like SerpApi does.
sentences.zh: Rose 表示，自 2023 年夏天（某种“API 末日”开始）以来，出版商一直在切断对开放网络的访问，试图找到快速阻止像 SerpApi 那样的大量 AI 抓取的方法。

blocks.html_en: “This mass reaction to scraping” has caused a “re-enclosure of a lot of the web,” Rose said. And concerningly, that doesn’t just gum up AI training efforts, it also harms research, archiving, journalism, public health reporting, and other important work that depends on anonymous crawling and automated scraping at scale, Rose said.

sentences.en: “This mass reaction to scraping” has caused a “re-enclosure of a lot of the web,” Rose said.
sentences.zh: 罗斯说，“这种对抓取的大规模反应”导致了“许多网络的重新封闭”。

sentences.en: And concerningly, that doesn’t just gum up AI training efforts, it also harms research, archiving, journalism, public health reporting, and other important work that depends on anonymous crawling and automated scraping at scale, Rose said.
sentences.zh: 罗斯说，令人担忧的是，这不仅会阻碍人工智能培训工作，还会损害研究、归档、新闻、公共卫生报告和其他依赖大规模匿名爬行和自动抓取的重要工作。

blocks.html_en: SerpApi told Ars that it has gotten “overwhelming” feedback from its customers, researchers, and SEO providers in support of its efforts to defend against the Google and Reddit lawsuits. The web scraper is optimistic that the court will grant its motion to dismiss against Reddit and last week celebrated that Google’s lawsuit may only proceed on very limited claims.

sentences.en: SerpApi told Ars that it has gotten “overwhelming” feedback from its customers, researchers, and SEO providers in support of its efforts to defend against the Google and Reddit lawsuits.
sentences.zh: SerpApi 告诉 Ars，它已经从客户、研究人员和 SEO 提供商那里得到了“压倒性”的反馈，以支持其抵御 Google 和 Reddit 诉讼的努力。

sentences.en: The web scraper is optimistic that the court will grant its motion to dismiss against Reddit and last week celebrated that Google’s lawsuit may only proceed on very limited claims.
sentences.zh: 该网络爬虫乐观地认为法院将批准驳回 Reddit 诉讼的动议，并于上周庆祝谷歌的诉讼可能只会针对非常有限的索赔进行。

blocks.html_en: In a win, SerpApi warned that Reddit planned to act as a “toll collector,” requiring payments for scraping when it doesn’t even own the content.

sentences.en: In a win, SerpApi warned that Reddit planned to act as a “toll collector,” requiring payments for scraping when it doesn’t even own the content.
sentences.zh: SerpApi 警告称，Reddit 计划充当“收费员”，在其不拥有内容的情况下要求为抓取付费。

blocks.html_en: “Reddit seeks to consolidate its control over its users’ content so that it will be in a better position to tax that content. Reddit is not acting to protect its users; Reddit is clearing a path to exploit them,” SerpApi warned.

sentences.en: “Reddit seeks to consolidate its control over its users’ content so that it will be in a better position to tax that content.
sentences.zh: “Reddit 寻求巩固对其用户内容的控制，以便能够更好地对这些内容征税。

sentences.en: Reddit is not acting to protect its users; Reddit is clearing a path to exploit them,” SerpApi warned.
sentences.zh: Reddit 并未采取行动保护其用户； Reddit 正在为利用它们扫清道路。”SerpApi 警告说。

blocks.html_en: Similarly, SerpApi accused Google of asking the court to ignore that it’s the “largest scraper on the planet,” while agreeing to cut off other web scrapers from information that is “100 percent public.”

sentences.en: Similarly, SerpApi accused Google of asking the court to ignore that it’s the “largest scraper on the planet,” while agreeing to cut off other web scrapers from information that is “100 percent public.”
sentences.zh: 同样，SerpApi 指责谷歌要求法院忽视它是“地球上最大的爬虫”，同时同意切断其他网络爬虫与“100％公开”信息的联系。

blocks.html_en: For Rose, there’s no winning for online users if, at the end of the fight, public access to data is cut off.

sentences.en: For Rose, there’s no winning for online users if, at the end of the fight, public access to data is cut off.
sentences.zh: 对于罗斯来说，如果在战斗结束时公众对数据的访问被切断，那么在线用户就不会获胜。

blocks.html_en: “It’s a very fraught time,” Rose said, acknowledging that it’s not just Reddit and Google but many publishers across the web that are currently tempted to use “whatever tool is available in the toolbox to tamper down” AI scraping.

sentences.en: “It’s a very fraught time,” Rose said, acknowledging that it’s not just Reddit and Google but many publishers across the web that are currently tempted to use “whatever tool is available in the toolbox to tamper down” AI scraping.
sentences.zh: 罗斯说：“这是一个非常令人担忧的时期。”他承认，不仅是 Reddit 和谷歌，网络上的许多出版商目前都试图使用“工具箱中可用的任何工具来篡改”人工智能抓取。

blocks.html_en: Some publishers may be financially motivated, like Google and Reddit, while others may be protecting their infrastructure or taking a moral stance, Rose said. Whatever the motivation is, “it’s leading to this kind of broader ecosystem-wide consequence of re-enclosure,” she warned.

sentences.en: Some publishers may be financially motivated, like Google and Reddit, while others may be protecting their infrastructure or taking a moral stance, Rose said.
sentences.zh: 罗斯说，一些出版商可能是出于经济动机，比如谷歌和 Reddit，而其他出版商可能是出于保护其基础设施或采取道德立场的目的。

sentences.en: Whatever the motivation is, “it’s leading to this kind of broader ecosystem-wide consequence of re-enclosure,” she warned.
sentences.zh: 无论动机是什么，“这都会导致重新圈地带来更广泛的生态系统后果，”她警告说。

blocks.html_en: And although SerpApi expects to win, the problem with DMCA cases, she suggested, is that it can be difficult to predict the outcome.

sentences.en: And although SerpApi expects to win, the problem with DMCA cases, she suggested, is that it can be difficult to predict the outcome.
sentences.zh: 她表示，尽管 SerpApi 预计会获胜，但 DMCA 案件的问题在于，很难预测结果。

blocks.html_en: “I’m very curious how this is going to play out with Reddit,” Rose said. “I’m always a little bit cynical because to some extent, whenever you get into the copyright realm, a lot of judges just decide it’s all vibes.”

sentences.en: “I’m very curious how this is going to play out with Reddit,” Rose said.
sentences.zh: “我很好奇这将如何在 Reddit 上发挥作用，”罗斯说。

sentences.en: “I’m always a little bit cynical because to some extent, whenever you get into the copyright realm, a lot of judges just decide it’s all vibes.”
sentences.zh: “我总是有点愤世嫉俗，因为在某种程度上，每当你进入版权领域，很多法官都会认为这都是共鸣。”

blocks.html_en: Advance Publications, which owns Ars Technica parent Condé Nast, is the largest shareholder in Reddit.

sentences.en: Advance Publications, which owns Ars Technica parent Condé Nast, is the largest shareholder in Reddit.
sentences.zh: Advance Publications 拥有 Ars Technica 母公司 Condé Nast，也是 Reddit 的最大股东。

blocks.html_en: Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

sentences.en: Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies.
sentences.zh: 阿什利 (Ashley) 是 Ars Technica 的高级政策记者，致力于追踪新兴政策和新技术的社会影响。

sentences.en: She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.
sentences.zh: 她是一位拥有 20 年经验的芝加哥记者。

content_html_zh:
隔离开放网络？

专家表示，谷歌和 Reddit 使用 DMCA 来对抗网络爬虫是很奇怪的。

上周在法庭上惨败后，谷歌确认不会放弃阻止人工智能机器人抓取其搜索结果的斗争。 Reddit 也奇怪地加入其中。

去年 12 月，谷歌奇怪地援引了《数字千年版权法》(DMCA)，起诉了 SerpApi。 这家搜索巨头指责网络抓取工具规避其反抓取技术，然后通过未经授权的“Google Search API”软件服务出售从 Google 搜索结果中抓取的内容。

据谷歌称，反抓取技术是为了保护搜索结果中受版权保护的内容。 据称，SerpApi 的规避行为可能会破坏谷歌与权利持有者的关系，其中包括一些向谷歌授权内容出现在所谓的“知识面板”中的人，这些面板显示在一些知名人士或实体的搜索结果中。

这是对 DMCA 的奇怪使用，因为 Google 搜索结果不受版权保护。 但在 Reddit 去年 10 月提起类似诉讼，指控 SerpApi 和 Google 竞争对手 Perplexity 抓取 Google 搜索结果中出现的 Reddit 内容后，Google 显然更有勇气探索法律理论。

谷歌在一篇博客中在宣布自己的挑战时引用了 Reddit 的诉讼，称该诉讼是阻止“恶意抓取”的“最后手段”，因为这些行为侵犯了权利人对谁可以访问其内容的选择。

具体来说，谷歌声称 SerpApi 的规避行为违反了其条款，使其无法从“数十亿”机器人搜索中获利或抵消其成本。 在此之前，Reddit 声称 SerpApi 规避了两个级别的安全性：Reddit 自己的控件阻止在其平台上抓取，而 Google 则控制阻止抓取搜索结果中的 Reddit 内容。

梅雷迪思·罗斯 (Meredith Rose) 是非营利性公共利益组织 Public Knowledge 的高级政策顾问，拥有 DMCA 方面的专业知识，她告诉 Ars，面对过去三年来突然、持续增长的人工智能抓取，谷歌和 Reddit 似乎“抓住了任何可用的工具”。 虽然他们使用 DMCA 的方式“很奇怪”——而且“不是法律所考虑的用例”——但她说这并不“令人惊讶”。 从历史上看，DMCA 一直是一种有效的工具，可以快速阻止不受欢迎的内容使用并强制围绕许可进行讨论，因此考虑到 Google 的目标，转向它可能是一个明显的起点。

但谷歌和 Reddit 不同寻常的 DMCA 论点似乎并没有获胜。 上周，法院采取了罕见的步骤，批准了 SerpApi 在谷歌诉讼中很早就提出的驳回动议。 在该案中，法官发现 Google 没有 DMCA 资格起诉 SerpApi，因为它不拥有搜索结果中的任何内容，也没有表明它代表任何权利所有者行事。

“这种情况并不经常发生，”罗斯告诉 Ars。 “这实际上可以归结为谷歌没有充分声明它所保护的内容是受版权保护的。”

对于 Reddit 来说，这一决定的时机可能不太好，上周四 Reddit 就 SerpApi 驳回诉讼的动议举行了听证会。 目前尚不清楚法院将如何裁决该案，但罗斯告诉 Ars，谷歌的裁决对 Reddit 来说不是好兆头，因为 Reddit 不能声称自己是搜索结果中内容的内容所有者或独家被许可人。

“谷歌案件的法官说，‘好吧，为了有资格根据 DMCA 提起诉讼，你可以是版权所有者或独家被许可人或正在部署和制造相关技术保护措施的人，’”Rose 告诉 Ars。 “Reddit 不是这些东西。”

SerpApi 希望这场斗争能够尽快结束，并告诉 Ars，为了捍卫开放网络，这场代价高昂的法律斗争值得坚持下去。

SerpApi 告诉 Ars：“最重要的是，谷歌和 Reddit 似乎都试图利用 DMCA 来隔离开放的互联网，追溯性地声称控制非他们创作且不拥有的内容。”

谷歌继续战斗的最后机会

尽管 Rose 同意 SerpApi 的观点，即在批准驳回动议时，法院给 SerpApi 带来了一场巨大的胜利，但斗争尚未结束，因为谷歌在继续打击网络抓取方面的道路很狭窄。

谷歌承认搜索结果不受版权保护，但辩称“知识面板”有时包括谷歌从权利持有者处许可的受版权保护的内容。 如果谷歌可以修改其投诉，声称权利持有者直接授权谷歌使用其反抓取技术来防止未经授权的内容访问，那么谷歌也许能够阻止非常有限的 SerpApi 抓取量。

谷歌发言人何塞·卡斯塔涅达 (José Castañeda) 告诉 Ars，谷歌计划修改起诉书，并“很高兴看到法院驳回了 SerpApi 几乎所有的法律论据”，否则试图对谷歌的地位提出质疑。

卡斯塔涅达表示：“我们期待按照法院的邀请提交修改后的申诉，并且我们仍然致力于保护我们的服务和合作伙伴免受未经授权的访问。”

然而，罗斯告诉 Ars，谷歌在某种程度上“无论是在这次诉讼中还是在历史上，都让自己陷入了困境”。

罗斯表示，对于谷歌来说，认为知识面板“充满了受版权保护的材料”可能是“非常危险的”。 罗斯表示，由于这家搜索巨头并未对知识盒中的所有内容进行许可，因此如果未经许可通过算法创建知识盒的行为突然被视为侵权，谷歌可能会面临未来诉讼的风险。

“他们必须以某种方式提出论点，其中的某些部分是受版权保护材料的复制品，但唯一属于受版权保护材料复制品的部分是他们明确许可的内容，”罗斯建议道。 “否则，他们就承认自己在未经许可的情况下复制了一些东西，这会让他们陷入另一场他们可能不希望发生的合理使用之争。”

谷歌有 21 天的时间来修改其投诉，届时它计划如何继续其 DMCA 斗争将变得更加清晰。

SerpApi 称战斗是“误导的”

Reddit 没有回应 Ars 的置评请求，但在上周听证会之前的一份文件中声称，它准备讨论谷歌的法庭败诉对其案件有何影响。

也许值得注意的是，SerpApi 表示 Reddit 并未出现在法庭的出席者之中。 SerpApi 没有对 Reddit 在听证会上的论点发表太多评论，但表示法官似乎专注于法律问题的细微差别。 最特别的是，法官似乎对 Reddit 与谷歌的协议是否实际上授权谷歌保护其受版权保护的内容感兴趣。

这样看来，两个法院都在一定程度上缩小了对这个关键问题的争论范围，但 SerpApi 似乎相信谷歌和 Reddit 都无法提供证据证明抓取公共搜索结果会损害权利人的利益。

当被问及对谷歌修改投诉的计划发表评论时，SerpApi 告诉 Ars，在谷歌发起攻击以保护搜索结果中出现的“数十万出版商”之后，继续争论“谷歌知识面板中出现的文本片段”可能没有什么意义。

SerpApi 表示：“我们希望谷歌放弃对开放互联网的这种误导性攻击，但如有必要，我们准备捍卫 SerpApi、我们的客户和我们的原则。”

SerpApi 告诉 Ars，在应对 DMCA 诉讼的同时，其业务仍在持续增长，但由于两起案件都拖延，其客户，包括 Nvidia、Uber 和 Adob​​e 等科技巨头，都面临着不确定性。

SerpApi 表示，他们“每天都依靠 SerpApi 提供对搜索数据的结构化访问，这一直是合法且合法的业务”。

专家称 SerpApi 有权捍卫开放网络

SerpApi 表示，除了自己的客户之外，投资开放网络的人们也在思考谷歌获胜可能带来的影响。

SerpApi 表示：“当然，诉讼成本高昂且具有破坏性。” “然而，我们强烈认为，谷歌和 Reddit 等平台并不拥有互联网，他们试图将 DMCA 武器化，威胁到开放网络的所有用户。”

Rose 告诉 Ars，虽然 SerpApi 不一定“受到很多人的喜爱”，但她认为“从政策角度来看，他们是正确的。”

Rose 表示，自 2023 年夏天（某种“API 末日”开始）以来，出版商一直在切断对开放网络的访问，试图找到快速阻止像 SerpApi 那样的大量 AI 抓取的方法。

罗斯说，“这种对抓取的大规模反应”导致了“许多网络的重新封闭”。 罗斯说，令人担忧的是，这不仅会阻碍人工智能培训工作，还会损害研究、归档、新闻、公共卫生报告和其他依赖大规模匿名爬行和自动抓取的重要工作。

SerpApi 告诉 Ars，它已经从客户、研究人员和 SEO 提供商那里得到了“压倒性”的反馈，以支持其抵御 Google 和 Reddit 诉讼的努力。 该网络爬虫乐观地认为法院将批准驳回 Reddit 诉讼的动议，并于上周庆祝谷歌的诉讼可能只会针对非常有限的索赔进行。

SerpApi 警告称，Reddit 计划充当“收费员”，在其不拥有内容的情况下要求为抓取付费。

“Reddit 寻求巩固对其用户内容的控制，以便能够更好地对这些内容征税。 Reddit 并未采取行动保护其用户； Reddit 正在为利用它们扫清道路。”SerpApi 警告说。

同样，SerpApi 指责谷歌要求法院忽视它是“地球上最大的爬虫”，同时同意切断其他网络爬虫与“100％公开”信息的联系。

对于罗斯来说，如果在战斗结束时公众对数据的访问被切断，那么在线用户就不会获胜。

罗斯说：“这是一个非常令人担忧的时期。”他承认，不仅是 Reddit 和谷歌，网络上的许多出版商目前都试图使用“工具箱中可用的任何工具来篡改”人工智能抓取。

罗斯说，一些出版商可能是出于经济动机，比如谷歌和 Reddit，而其他出版商可能是出于保护其基础设施或采取道德立场的目的。 无论动机是什么，“这都会导致重新圈地带来更广泛的生态系统后果，”她警告说。

她表示，尽管 SerpApi 预计会获胜，但 DMCA 案件的问题在于，很难预测结果。

“我很好奇这将如何在 Reddit 上发挥作用，”罗斯说。 “我总是有点愤世嫉俗，因为在某种程度上，每当你进入版权领域，很多法官都会认为这都是共鸣。”

Advance Publications 拥有 Ars Technica 母公司 Condé Nast，也是 Reddit 的最大股东。

阿什利 (Ashley) 是 Ars Technica 的高级政策记者，致力于追踪新兴政策和新技术的社会影响。 她是一位拥有 20 年经验的芝加哥记者。
